messages:
alex: kicking off a short ramp in staging to validate per-key burst controls + fallback routing. 30m window, ramp to 500 rps, then a steady 200 rps soak. want to catch cache/KV refill and leaky-bucket edgecases.

maya: thanks. which quota model are we testing — per-key only, per-org, or hybrid?

alex: hybrid. primary enforcement is per-key with an org-level cap as a backstop. config snippet: 
```json
{
  \"quota_policy\": \"hybrid\",
  \"per_key\": { \"burst_tokens\": 100, \"refill_per_sec\": 5 },
  \"per_org\": { \"burst_tokens\": 10000, \"refill_per_sec\": 200 }
}
```

chen: noted — telemetry checklist: token-bucket fill, drops by rule, route-fallback counts, and distinct per-key histograms. I'll add panels. link: https://grafana.redwood/staging/d/ql/quota-playback (will add queries in a min)

jess: also include a panel for request id -> key mapping so we can spot hot keys. we saw weird hotkey reconstructions last week.

sam: FYI there's an existing subtle bug where refill math uses integer seconds and misses subsecond bursts. reproduced locally:
```
[2026-10-12T14:03:02Z] key=acct:123 consumed=120 tokens remaining=-20 -> should have been 0 after refill window
```
we should exercise short burst spikes to trigger that.

alex: good call. test plan: generate 10k unique api-keys + 50 hot keys (to stress long tail). traffic mix: 70% single-shot gen, 20% streaming, 10% embedding. will use traffic-bot (chaos-proxy) to replay.

maya: can you also enable routing policy fallback to model-lite for 5% of excess traffic so we can validate graceful degradation? e.g., route to gptx-small when per-key throttled.

alex: yes — fallback rule enabled: route.policy = \"fallback_to_compatible\" with model whitelist [gptx-small,v1]. When throttled, returns 429+X-Fallback-Route header and attempts retry to fallback.

ops-bot: deploy job #deploy-4898 started by alex — applying quota config to staging (namespaces: staging-eu, staging-us).

chen: added Grafana panels: \"quota.leaky_bucket_fill\", \"quota.enforcement.counts\", \"routing.fallback.attempts\". queries use tag:key for per-key breakdown. will share snapshots after first run.

jess: question for design: UX in console — should we surface per-key burst tokens remaining in the keys table? that might be noisy for org admins.

sam: I'd prefer an events view (time-series) + a single numeric in the table (e.g., current refill rate). full token stream in the key detail page.

alex: ok. action items: 1) run #1 now (10m ramp + 20m soak) — i'm starting traffic-bot. 2) maya to watch throttles and confirm fallback counts. 3) chen to snapshot dashboards. 4) sam to run leak/refill repro if failure seen and open CORE ticket. 5) jess to draft a quick console mock of per-key detail.

maya: running watch now. will post quick logs if anomalies.

[~2m later]

maya: initial run hit target QPS. seeing a small spike in per-key 429s concentrated on 50 hot keys. fallback attempts ~120 over the ramp window. charts look clean but refill distribution is slightly off for subsecond spikes. attaching short log:
```
2026-10-12T14:08:23Z key=acct:hot42 event=throttle returned=429 fallback_attempt=1 route=gptx-small
2026-10-12T14:08:24Z key=acct:hot42 event=replay_to_fallback result=200 latency_ms=85
```

sam: that matches my local. I'll push a tiny patch to refine refill to use sliding-window subsecond math. if anyone objects, speak now.

jess: go ahead. we need that fix before any canary.

alex: agreed. we'll pause further runs until patch lands. once merged, re-run full 30m test with mixed org-level burst (simulate a tenant spike).

chen: created ticket CORE-5123 for refill precision + test case. assigned to sam.

alex: thanks team. will update thread when we re-run. :thumbsup:
